messages:
Ava: Quick sync — post-launch snapshot. Metrics look stable overall but we have a consistent p95 latency regression for long prompts (~4% increase) and two customer-facing bugs reported. Proposing a focused 2-week follow-up: immediate hotfix for P1/P2, then a small enhancement wave for caching and prompt-guidance. :eyes:
Jon: Saw the spike in traces. Root looks like batching/backpressure under long-seq workloads. I can scope a targeted fix that tightens batch timeouts + adds a safety-kv-evict. ETA for a PR today.
Marta: I can do an infra-side quick patch to autoscaler and throttling windows to reduce contention. Will coordinate the temporary capacity bump for canary.
Ava: Cool. Let's be explicit on priority rules so grooming is fast: P0 = data-loss or correctness failures; P1 = customer-facing errors causing tasks to fail; P2 = perf regressions impacting p95 latency > 200ms; P3 = UX/feature polish. Anything not P0-P2 goes to the enhancement wave.
Priya: From PMM/customer signals — three customers asked for deterministic token-cost reporting and one asked for streaming stability. Those map to P2 (streaming), P3 (token UI). Worth flagging the token-cost ask for the enhancement batch.
Evan: Design can prepare a small prompt-guidance doc and a compact UI mock for token-cost later this sprint. No big scope needed.
Jon: For the hotfix, plan is: tighten batch timeout from 30ms -> 15ms, add an extra KV cache eviction on long prompt paths, and guard the retry path to avoid duplicate in-flight requests. I'll open a PR titled "batching: short-timeout + kv-guard" and link test vectors.
Ava: Good. Acceptance criteria for the hotfix: 1) reduce p95 on long prompts by >= 50% of regression (measured vs baseline), 2) no increase in error rate, 3) end-to-end tests for the retry guard. If all pass, do a canary deploy then full rollout.
Marta: Canary plan I suggest: 5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100%, wait 1h between steps for perf signal. If p95 > baseline+50ms or error rate increases by >0.5% revert. I'll run a short smoke harness during each step.
Ava: Let's publish that plan in the release checklist. Also we need a grooming slot tomorrow to triage backlog items into hotfix vs enhancement. Suggest 30m async thread + 30m live triage.
Priya: I'll prepare customer-impact notes for the three named customers and rank urgency. I'll also draft messaging for those on the early-adopter list if we need a hotfix rollout.
Jon: Test plan: unit + integration + a small replay test using the production prompt sample set. I'll pin the test run command in the PR: ```./scripts/replay_prompts.sh --sample recent_long_prompts --retries 0```
Marta: FYI I kicked a temporary capacity bump for the next 6h in us-west to reduce noise during PR validation. Will revert after canary finishes.
Ava: Timeline: PR by EOD, review + tests next day, canary the day after. If green, ship within 72h. Enhancement wave (token-cost UI + prompt hints + docs) targeted for next micro-sprint (week after).
Jon: Noted. I'll include a changelog entry and a simple migration note (no data migrations).
Priya: For prioritization rubric during grooming tomorrow: customer-reported + frequency + revenue impact; anything with >1 customer and severity >=P2 goes to hotfix. Others to enhancement backlog with a target milestone.
Evan: I'll attach the design sketches and copy for the token-cost modal in the grooming thread.
Ava: Perfect. Final ask: everyone add one-line owner and blocker to the async doc before 10am tomorrow. We'll meet 10:30 for the 30m triage. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled by Marta at 2026-03-22T14:00Z (5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100%). Monitoring hooks: perf-stream, errors, throughput.
Jon: Thanks — I'll watch the traces during canary and be on-call for revert.
Marta: Will post status updates in #product and #eng-oncall during the rollout.
Ava: Awesome team. We'll close the loop in this thread after canary. :shipit:
